battle.name: 十二月黨人起義
battle.brief: 一八二五年十二月十一日起，聖彼得堡近衛軍與海軍禁衛隊部分官兵在京基院前集結，因亞歷山大一世猝逝後的繼承權爭議，挾炮兵與海軍水兵攻入冬宮，要求宣布康斯坦丁一世即位。三日之內近衛炮兵以霰彈驅散廣場叛軍，起義即告瓦解；卡面火繩槍銃所代表的舊式輕型火槍血統，正是已由燧發步槍取代的裝備。

kit.name: 火繩槍銃
kit.history: 比步槍輕的長槍。西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲。

countries: 這不是國家對國家的國際戰爭，而是俄羅斯帝國軍隊內部一場政治性武裝叛亂，與王朝方面的平叛之間的對抗。叛軍一方由秘密社團北方協會與南方協會的核心成員在聖彼得堡臨時拼合而成，軍事骨幹來自近衛軍系統：聖彼得堡近衛步兵團與諾夫哥羅德近衛步兵團的部分官兵、海軍禁衛隊第一與第二營的水兵，以及莫斯科總參謀部軍官學校和海軍軍校的學員。北方協會原本計劃在涅瓦河畔平原打一場「會戰」，南方協會的方案則是讓自己掌握的團級單位向彼得堡行軍會戰；十二月十一日，兩個計畫尚未合併，首都的行動便提前爆發。政府一方是尼古拉一世本人與帝國最高權力機構：御前會議、樞密院與總參謀部在叛軍要求宣布康斯坦丁一世即位時一致拒絕；禁衛總指揮兼御前侍從長 A. X. 別克恩多夫少將主持平叛，陸軍大臣基謝列夫元帥接管首都防務，御前大臣戈爾恰科夫公爵執行宮廷戒嚴，近衛炮兵連與近衛騎兵巡邏封鎖街道、橋樑以及通往皇村的道路。樞密院廣場與冬宮之間的衝突，成為帝國軍令系統與一群軍官陰謀之間最直接的一次對撞。
countriesEn: This was not a war between states but a political insurrection inside the armed forces of the Russian Empire and the dynasty's suppression of it. The rebel side was an ad hoc coalition of the Northern and Southern Societies pieced together in St Petersburg; its military skeleton came from the Guards system — parts of the St Petersburg Grenadier Regiment and the Novgorod Grenadier Regiment, the sailors of the first and second battalions of the Naval Guard, and the cadets of the Moscow General Staff Officer School and the Naval Cadet Corps. The Northern Society had planned to fight a pitched battle on the plain by the Neva, while the Southern Society's scheme called for the regiments it controlled to march on Petersburg and win a set-piece engagement; the two plans had not been merged when the capital action broke out early on the night of 11 December. On the government side stood Nicholas I himself and the empire's highest authorities: the State Council, the Senate and the General Staff unanimously refused the rebels' demand that Constantine be proclaimed. The overall command of the suppression lay with Lieutenant General Alexander von Benckendorff, commander of the Guards and head of the Imperial Chancellery; Count Peter Kiselev, Minister of War, took charge of the capital's defence; Alexander Gorchakov, Minister of the Imperial Court, enforced the palace martial law; batteries of the Guards Artillery and patrols of the Guard cavalry closed the streets, the bridges and the road to Tsarskoye Selo. The clash between Senate Square and the Winter Palace became the most direct collision yet between the imperial command system and a conspiracy of officers.
people: 叛軍的策劃與指揮核心，是一批二十多歲至四十歲之間的帝國軍官與知識分子。北方協會主席謝爾蓋·特魯別茨科伊公爵，在十一月最後一週才被推舉接替已被流放的伊拉里昂·多羅霍托夫；著名軍事起草者帕維爾·佩斯捷爾少校在《俄羅斯真理》草案中提出廢除帝制、建立共和國，並以土地分配與奴隸解放為綱領；尼克伊塔·穆拉維約夫擬定以「國家杜馬」為核心的憲法方案，被視為最接近可實行藍圖的一派；米哈伊爾·盧寧則是敢於在冬宮前公開宣讀宣言的人。軍中真正發動起事的是炮兵中校阿爾塔蒙·扎哈羅夫與近衛軍中尉謝爾蓋·穆拉維約夫-阿波斯托爾；海軍軍校出身的詩人康德拉季·雷列耶夫參與起草北方協會的宣言。信號總是錯時：彼得堡要塞上的火盆因暴風無法點燃，起義從深夜拖到上午。政府方面的關鍵人物是別克恩多夫少將，他在總參謀部與冬宮之間護送尼古拉一世脫身並組織戒嚴；米哈伊爾·斯佩蘭斯基受命主持特別調查委員會，而五名主犯的死刑則由沙皇親自核准。
peopleEn: The core of the conspiracy was a group of imperial officers and intellectuals in their twenties and thirties. Prince Sergei Trubetskoy, president of the Northern Society, was elected only in the last week of November to replace Ilarion Dorokhov, who had already been exiled; the military theorist Pavel Pestel, a lieutenant, set out in the draft 'Russkaya Pravda' a republic without an emperor, with land distribution and the freeing of serfs at its core; Nikita Muravyov drew up a constitutional scheme built around a national Duma, and was regarded as the closest thing to a workable programme; Mikhail Lunin was the man willing to read the declaration aloud in front of the Winter Palace. The officers who actually set the revolt in motion were Artillery Colonel Artamon Zakharov and Guards Lieutenant Sergei Muravyov-Apostol; Kondraty Ryleyev, the poet and a naval cadet, took part in drafting the Northern Society's declaration. The signals always failed: the brazier on the Peter and Paul Fortress could not be lit in the storm, and the rising dragged from the small hours into the morning. On the government side the key figure was Benckendorff, who escorted Nicholas I from the General Staff building to safety and organised the cordon; Mikhail Speransky was given the chair of the special commission of inquiry, and the sentences of death on the five principal defendants were confirmed by the Emperor himself.
kits: 卡面這件火繩槍銃是十六世紀西班牙的輕型長槍，用火繩機構擊發，槍身比制式步槍輕、槍管細長，在西班牙的美洲殖民地曾大量配發給民兵與步兵。一八二五年十二月，帝國軍隊早已不用它：近衛軍與各步兵團裝備的是一八一一年式燧發滑膛步槍（通稱「刀形」式，配刺刀）、供散兵使用的一八〇八年式較輕步槍以及一八二〇式燧發槍，軍官則攜帶燧發手槍與短管騎槍。火繩槍銃在這個時代的實際位置，是軍械庫中作為舊式槍械的樣槍與儀仗陳列，以及軍人對「舊式輕型火槍」這一血統的稱呼。叛軍把火槍當作暴動的骨幹：北方協會計劃在涅瓦河畔以密集的線式射擊迎戰政府軍，佩斯捷爾的《俄羅斯真理》則描繪以土地軍與民兵為主體的未來共和國；南方協會的計畫同樣以火槍射擊作為主要火力。起義當日，叛軍從近衛步兵團的軍械庫取走步槍與刺刀，海軍禁衛隊水兵帶來營內的火槍，並試圖把涅瓦河一帶的野戰炮拖上街頭；冬宮廣場前的炮兵打算以實心彈與霰彈射擊政府軍，而近衛炮兵連在下午以野戰炮發射霰彈平射，把廣場上密集的叛軍隊形驅散。
kitsEn: The card's weapon, the Spanish matchlock arquebus of the sixteenth century, was a light long gun fired by a burning cord, lighter than a musket of the line and slender in the barrel, and it was issued in large numbers to the militias and infantry of Spain's American colonies. By December 1825 the Imperial army had long stopped using it: the Guards and the line infantry carried the 1811-pattern flintlock musket, the 'klinok' with its bayonet, together with the lighter 1808-pattern musket for skirmishers and the 1820-pattern flintlock gun, while officers carried flintlock pistols and short carbines. The arquebus's real place in 1825 was as a pattern piece and a ceremonial relic in the arsenals, and as the name by which soldiers still referred to the older light-gun lineage. The rebels treated muskets as the skeleton of an insurrection: the Northern Society planned to meet the government troops with dense linear fire on the Neva plain, and Pestel's 'Russkaya Pravda' projected a future republic built on a land army and a militia; the Southern Society's scheme likewise rested on musket fire as the main source of damage. On the day itself the rebels drew muskets and bayonets from the regimental stores of the Guards infantry, the Naval Guard sailors brought their battalion muskets and attempted to drag field guns up from the Neva; the rebel artillery before the Winter Palace meant to fire solid shot and canister on the government troops, while in the afternoon the Guards Artillery answered with canister from field pieces and scattered the dense columns in Palace Square.
tactics: 整套行動屬於十九世紀初帝國軍隊內部密謀的典型模式：以彼得堡要塞的火炮信號為總攻令，突襲冬宮，在部隊內部同時展開政治宣傳，散發宣言，要求士兵拒絕向康斯坦丁一世宣誓、轉而效忠「真正的君主」；北方協會的作戰計畫還寫明要在涅瓦河畔平原打一場「會戰」，以南軍與民兵取得決定性勝利為前提，南方協會則規劃所掌握的團隊分批向彼得堡行軍，用正面射擊與刺刀突破政府軍。實際執行卻因準備不足而全面失序：信號在暴風中延誤，起義從夜半拖到上午；聖彼得堡近衛步兵團只有部分連隊響應，諾夫哥羅德近衛步兵團在城外營區待命而未能及時趕到；宣讀宣言時士兵並未跟隨叛軍，多數軍官骨幹拒絕聽令。宮廷內部出現街頭混戰，軍官學校學員、冬宮衛兵與叛軍在庭院和柱廊下以刺刀相搏；叛軍還備有縱火燒毀冬宮的物資。傍晚近衛騎兵巡邏封鎖街口，近衛炮兵以野戰炮發射霰彈驅散廣場隊形，天黑之後叛軍自行潰散。
tacticsEn: The whole operation followed the classic pattern of a conspiracy inside an army: the signal was to be a salute fired from the Peter and Paul Fortress, the Winter Palace was to be seized by surprise, political propaganda was to be carried on simultaneously among the ranks, and manifestos were to be distributed urging soldiers to refuse the oath to Constantine and to serve instead the 'true sovereign'. The Northern Society's operational paper also specified a pitched battle on the plain by the Neva, premised on a decisive victory by the southern regiments and the militia, and the Southern Society planned a march of the units it controlled on Petersburg, breaking the government lines with disciplined fire and the bayonet. In execution everything went wrong: the signal was delayed by the storm, the rising dragged from midnight into the morning; only part of the St Petersburg Grenadier Regiment answered the call and the Novgorod Grenadier Regiment, waiting in its camp outside the capital, never arrived in time; when the declarations were read the ranks did not follow, and most of the officer corps refused orders. Inside the palace there was street fighting, cadets, Winter Palace guards and rebels struggling with bayonets in the courtyards and colonnades, and the rebels had materials ready for burning the palace down. In the evening patrols of the guard cavalry sealed the approaches, batteries of the Guards Artillery fired canister from field pieces over the square, and the columns fell apart as the light went.
data: 可考的數字並不完整，須逐一分辨。起義在舊曆十二月十一日夜間爆發，十二日清晨叛軍攻入冬宮，經十二日、十三日兩天的對峙，至十四日政府發表詔令宣示平定成功（新曆十二月二十三日至二十六日）。亞歷山大一世於十二月一日在塔甘羅格病逝，尼古拉一世在十二月二日即位，宣布康斯坦丁放棄王位、公告尼古拉繼承的欽命直到十二月六日才發出；新近招募的諾夫哥羅德近衛步兵團的士兵尚未重新宣誓，因而在起義當夜即被捲入。叛軍在首都可集合的兵力，軍官學校學員、海軍禁衛隊水兵與近衛步兵團部分官兵合計約三千人，其中在冬宮一帶集結者通常認為在一千五百至兩千人之間；政府方面第二日調集的鎮壓部隊，連同近衛騎兵、炮兵與首都各駐軍，達萬人量級。街頭戰鬥造成的雙方死亡人數史載不一，多數記述認為在數十人上下。事後被拘捕者逾三千人，特別調查委員會傳訊、審訊的嫌犯超過一千人，正式起訴八十六人；五名主犯處以死刑，一百二十餘人流放西伯利亞鄂嫩斯克礦區與赤塔要塞，其中數十餘人死於流放地。
dataEn: The record of numbers is incomplete and has to be handled with care. The rising broke out on the night of 11 December Old Style; the rebels entered the Winter Palace on the morning of the 12th, and after the confrontations of the 12th and 13th the government published a manifesto announcing the suppression on the 14th, that is 23 to 26 December New Style. Alexander I died at Taganrog on 1 December, Nicholas I acceded on 2 December, and the manifesto announcing Constantine's renunciation and Nicholas's accession was not issued until 6 December; the newly raised Novgorod Grenadier Regiment, whose recruits had not yet been re-sworn, was drawn in on the very night of the rising. The strength the rebels could assemble in the capital — cadets, Naval Guard sailors and parts of the Guards infantry — amounted to some three thousand men, of whom perhaps one thousand five hundred to two thousand were massed around the Winter Palace. On the government side, the troops brought in on the second day, together with the Guard cavalry, the artillery and the various garrison units of the capital, ran to a force of the order of ten thousand. The number killed in the street fighting is variously given and generally put at a few dozen. More than three thousand people were arrested afterwards; the commission of inquiry questioned over a thousand suspects and brought formal charges against eighty-six. Five of the principal defendants were sentenced to death, more than a hundred to penal servitude in the Nerchinsk mining district and the Chita prison, and several dozen of the exiles died in exile.
cause: 直接導火線是王位繼承的混亂。亞歷山大一世晚年的讓位嘗試，使一七九九年兄弟二人互許彼此不受侵犯的誓言與一八一二年的御令成為軍隊效忠對象的依據；本人病逝後，總參謀部與樞密院一度仍以康斯坦丁為繼承人，軍中高級將校隨即向康斯坦丁宣誓，消息傳到連隊後，許多士兵以為康斯坦丁才是君主而拒絕向尼古拉宣誓。御前會議、樞密院與總參謀部的一致拒絕、禁衛軍對宮廷的效忠，以及十二月初的公告，把一場原本捲入大批士兵的危機，壓成一場只能靠奪取宮廷才能解決的武裝政變；康斯坦丁本人則在一八二二年因與波蘭貴婦的低門第婚姻而自願放棄王位，坊間於是流傳他不願再登「滴血的寶座」之說。深層原因則是改革的天花板：解放戰爭與一八一二年的自由主義思潮在克里米亞戰敗後被壓回地下，秘密協會由一八一六年的「救濟同盟」、一八一八年的「福祉同盟」幾經重組，最終在一八二一年分裂為南方與北方兩會，一八二三年春兩會方約定共同武裝起事；佩斯捷爾《俄羅斯真理》的共和方案得不到任何武裝支持，穆拉維約夫的憲法草案與北方協會的君主立憲方案也無法在軍中取得共同綱領，亞歷山大一世對佩斯捷爾一八二〇年的請願書不作答覆，使志士們相信唯有自行奪取權力才能推行改革。
causeEn: The immediate spark was the confusion over the succession. Alexander I's late attempts to set the question of the crown aside, the oath of 1799 by which the two brothers promised to respect each other's rights, and the manifesto of 1812 had all become the basis of the army's allegiance; after the Emperor's death the General Staff and the Senate still treated Constantine as the heir, the senior officers of the army took the oath to Constantine, and the news reached the companies, so that many soldiers believed Constantine to be the sovereign and refused the oath to Nicholas. The unanimity of the State Council, the Senate and the General Staff in refusing the rebels, the loyalty of the Guards to the court and the manifesto of early December turned what might have been a mutiny of a whole army into an armed coup that could only be won by seizing the palace; Constantine himself had voluntarily renounced the crown in 1822 after a morganatic marriage to a Polish countess, and it was said in the cities that he would not mount the 'gory throne' again. The deeper cause was the ceiling on reform: the liberal sentiment of the Napoleonic years was driven underground after the defeat in the Crimea; the secret unions — the Union of Salvation of 1816, the Union of Welfare of 1818 — were reorganised several times and finally split in 1821 into a Southern and a Northern Society, which in the spring of 1823 agreed on a joint armed rising. Pestel's republican programme of the 'Russkaya Pravda' won no armed support, Muravyov's constitutional draft and the Northern Society's monarchical project could not agree on a common programme in the army, and Alexander's silence on Pestel's petition of 1820 convinced the conspirators that reform could be achieved only by seizing power themselves.
impact: 平叛成功的直接後果是鎮壓與政治轉向。一八二六年一月，沙皇成立以斯佩蘭斯基為主席的特別調查委員會，審訊範圍覆蓋數千名被拘者與上千名受訊者；七月十三日，五名主犯雷列耶夫、謝爾蓋·穆拉維約夫-阿波斯托爾、佩斯捷爾、別斯圖熱夫-雷明與彼得·穆拉維約夫-阿波斯托爾在聖彼得堡被公開絞刑，佩斯捷爾與雷列耶夫的遺體送解剖學院供解剖，數百名被判流放者在西伯利亞的鄂嫩斯克礦區與赤塔要塞死亡或在苦役中終身殘廢。制度上，尼古拉一世於一八二六年設立「御前辦公廳第三處」，由別克恩多夫直接掌管，成為俄羅斯第一個常設秘密警察機構；此後十年，書刊檢查、密探、告密與「可疑言論」的刑責被寫入法典，北方與南方協會被宣佈非法。觀念上，歐洲的自由派與激進派卻把「十二月黨人」視為俄羅斯改革的先聲：起義失敗的震撼成為十九世紀俄羅斯文學的長久母題，萊蒙托夫與普希金的詩作、托爾斯泰《戰爭與和平》中對一八一二年前後那段時光的回望，都不斷重提這批人。從長遠看，起義並未改變制度，卻在知識界留下一份無法清帳的道德債：一八二六年被史家視為俄國自由主義革命運動的鐘聲，此後的愛國者、自由主義者、民粹派與社會主義者皆以一八二五年為譜系起點，蘇俄更以「十二月黨人起義一百週年」為由全國慶祝，樞密院廣場改名為十二月黨人廣場，紀念碑上鐫刻「十二月黨人——後世感激的見證」之語。可以說，制度層面它是一次失敗，觀念層面它是一份未兌現的清單。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the successful suppression was terror and a turn towards reaction. In January 1826 the Emperor set up the special commission of inquiry under Speransky, whose enquiries covered thousands of arrests and more than a thousand interrogations; on 13 July five of the principal defendants — Ryleyev, Sergei Muravyov-Apostol, Pestel, Bestuzhev-Ryumin and Pyotr Muravyov-Apostol — were publicly hanged in St Petersburg, the bodies of Pestel and Ryleyev being handed to the Medical and Surgical Academy for dissection, while a number of those condemned perished or were permanently broken by hard labour in Nerchinsk and Chita. Institutionally, Nicholas created the Third Section of His Imperial Majesty's Own Chancellery in 1826, placed under Benckendorff, the first standing secret police in Russia; throughout the following decade censorship, agents, denunciation and liability for 'unclear words' were written into the statutes, and the Northern and Southern Societies were declared illegal. In the realm of ideas, the liberals and radicals of Europe took the 'Decembrists' for the herald of Russian reform: the shock of the failure became a lasting motif of Russian literature, revisited in Lermontov's and Pushkin's verse and in the reflections on the Napoleonic years in Tolstoy's 'War and Peace'. In the long run the rising changed no institutions, but it left an unpayable moral debt in the educated public: 1825 was sounded as the bell of the Russian liberal revolutionary movement, the patriots, liberals, populists and socialists of the later century took 1825 as their genealogical starting point, and the Soviet state marked the centenary with national celebration, renaming Senate Square the Decembrists' Square and setting on its monument the words that the Decembrists are the witness of a grateful posterity. In institutional terms it was a failure; in the realm of ideas, a list of promises handed down.
result: 結果是徹底的失敗，但失敗的意義被後世放大。起義在彼得堡只維持了三天：叛軍一度佔領冬宮、奪得宣言與部分軍械，卻無法讓普通士兵跟隨，沒有得到任何師以上的部隊配合，缺少足夠的彈藥與糧食補給，也拿不出可以立刻兌現的士兵物質訴求；佩斯捷爾的共和綱領、穆拉維約夫的憲法藍圖與北方協會的起義計畫，三者互不相容，結果只有別人的計畫在首都被倉促執行。北方協會在起義中扮演主導，卻沒有自保的武裝與足夠的準備；南方協會因起義提前爆發而失去集結的時間，其原有的「共和國」方案連一個模範營都沒有真正建起來。直接效應是沙皇政府以「第三處」加強特務警察，監督出版物與高等學校，官方把這場事件定名為「叛亂」並抹去其政治綱領；此後數十年，少壯知識分子的地下小組仍沿用「十二月黨人」的名號行動。從軍事史上看，三天的失敗提供了三條教訓：政治綱領必須先於奪權、奪權必須有基層的物質訴求，而機密組織的紀律在小規模城市起事中會被內部矛盾與時間失誤吃掉；這些教訓在克里米亞戰敗、一八六一年改革與一九〇五年革命中一再被重提。從政治史上看，制度的危機並未被解決：一八二六年之後是尼古拉一世以官僚、軍人與警察為骨幹的保守時期，真正的改革要等到一八六一年才重新出現在日程上。
resultEn: The result was an outright failure whose meaning was magnified afterwards. The rising lasted only three days in Petersburg: the rebels for a moment held the Winter Palace and seized the declarations and part of the regimental stores, but they could not carry the ranks with them, drew no support from any formation larger than a regiment, lacked ammunition and food, and had no material grievance the rank and file could immediately feel. Pestel's republican programme, Muravyov's constitutional scheme and the Northern Society's plan of operations were mutually incompatible, and in the end only somebody else's plan was hastily executed in the capital. The Northern Society had led the rising, yet had neither arms to defend itself nor preparation to match; the Southern Society, caught by the early outbreak, lost the time it needed to muster, and its project for a 'republic' never built so much as a model camp. The immediate effects were the Third Section, the tightening of police surveillance over the press and the universities, and the official relabelling of the rising as a 'mutiny' stripped of its political programme; for decades afterwards small underground groups of young intellectuals still acted under the name of the Decembrists. Military history draws three lessons from those three days: a political programme must precede the seizure of power, a seizure of power needs a material grievance the rank and file can feel, and the discipline of a clandestine association is eaten away by internal contradictions and lost time even in a small urban rising — lessons rehearsed again and again after the Crimean defeat, in the reforms of 1861 and in the revolution of 1905. Politically nothing was solved: the years of Nicholas I after 1826 were a conservative period built on bureaucracy, army and police, and real reform did not return to the agenda until 1861.
